text: dsh-email（DSH 插件，适用于支持 DSH 工具的客户端）：通过一个 email 工具连接已配置的 IMAP/SMTP 邮箱。它可列出、搜索和阅读邮件，管理邮件标记与文件夹，保存附件，并发送、回复或转发邮件；可选的新邮件触发器会为新邮件启动 agent 会话。适合希望让 DSH agent 协助处理邮箱的用户。需要配置邮箱登录名、密码或应用专用密码，以及 IMAP/SMTP 主机。

dsh-email connects DSH to configured IMAP/SMTP mailboxes through an email tool. It can search, read, and organize mail, save attachments, and send, reply to, or forward messages. An optional trigger starts an agent session for new mail. It needs mailbox credentials and IMAP/SMTP hosts.
想讓 DSH agent 幫我查郵件並草擬回覆。
需要從 agent 搜尋收件匣、讀取郵件和附件。
I want an agent to send and reply to email from my configured mailbox.
dsh-email 的功能「邮件查阅与搜索」：通过 email 工具分页列出、筛选或搜索邮件摘要，并读取指定邮件正文和附件信息。调用 list、list_unseen、search 或 read，内容来自配置账户的 IMAP 邮箱。
dsh-email 的功能「发送和回复邮件」：通过 email 工具发送新邮件、回复或转发指定邮件，可填写收件人、正文及本地附件；配置 SENT_FOLDER 时还可复制已发送邮件。
dsh-email 使用前须知：邮件读写通过每个账户配置的 IMAP/SMTP 主机进行；新邮件触发开启时，邮件发件人、主题和可用正文会传入新建的 DSH agent 会话。账户配置需要密码或应用专用密码。
dsh-email 的维护与更新元数据：活跃维护；距最后推送 26 天；提交数 16；更新频次 unknown；近 90 天提交 未知；开放 Issue 未知；仓库健康分 62/100（置信度 low）。

dsh-email README · dsh-email：dsh-email gives a DSH agent working access to a mailbox: the `email` tool reads and sends the user's mail over standard IMAP/SMTP, so the agent can check and answer it with only a password or app-specific password.

dsh-email README · dsh-email：- Read and search mail: list, unread view, structured search, read without marking seen
- Verify account health: verify checks every configured account live (IMAP login + SMTP authentication) with zero side effects
- Send, reply, forward - with attachments
- Manage mailboxes: create and delete folders, move messages
- Multiple accounts in one plugin
- Deletion is per-account gated: delete and delete_folder run only on accounts that opt in
- Optional new-mail trigger: a per-account resident watcher dispatches a fresh agent session per new mail, running an operator-defined policy prompt
- Session offload: a per-minute sweep archives settled trigger sessions that outlived their account's retention window (env-only: EMAIL_<N>_SESSION_RETENTION), keeping the framework session store bounded
- Stateless verbs: one fresh connection per call (the trigger watcher is the only resident connection, only on enabled accounts)

dsh-email README · Installation：dsh-email is an out-of-tree plugin for a dsh profile. Install it with the dsh plugin command:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add dsh-email
```

Configuration is layered: built-in defaults, the `EMAIL_*` env block, and a
cordis config layer (see below); the plugin creates no config or state files
in the profile directory (its only on-disk state is the session offload's
retention log and archive under `$DSH_HOME/dsh-email/`, used only by the
trigger plane, see Session offload).

dsh-email README · Configuration：The env block is static per process boot; env changes take effect on a host
restart. One account needs four variables, the rest are optional:

dsh-email README · Configuration：| Variable | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `EMAIL_<N>_USER` | yes | login name shared by IMAP and SMTP (usually the mailbox address) |
| `EMAIL_<N>_PASS` | yes | password or the provider's app-specific password / auth code |
| `EMAIL_<N>_IMAP_HOST` | yes | IMAP server host |
| `EMAIL_<N>_IMAP_PORT` | no | IMAP port, default 993 |
| `EMAIL_<N>_IMAP_SECURE` | no | IMAP TLS mode: `tls` = implicit TLS / `starttls` = mandatory STARTTLS upgrade / `none` = full plaintext, no STARTTLS attempted; default `tls` |
| `EMAIL_<N>_IMAP_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS` | no | certificate validation: `false` = strict (default) / `true` = accept untrusted / self-signed certificates (only meaningful with the `tls` / `starttls` modes) |
| `EMAIL_<N>_SMTP_HOST` | yes | SMTP server host |
| `EMAIL_<N>_SMTP_PORT` | no | SMTP port, default 587 |
| `EMAIL_<N>_SMTP_SECURE` | no | SMTP TLS mode: the same three values as the IMAP side; default `starttls` |
| `EMAIL_<N>_SMTP_ALLOW_INSECURE_TLS` | no | same as the IMAP side |
| `EMAIL_<N>_FROM` | no | sender address, default = `EMAIL_<N>_USER` |
| `EMAIL_<N>_FROM_NAME` | no | sender display name |
| `EMAIL_<N>_SENT_FOLDER` | no | when

dsh-email README · Configuration：The `<N>` segment is the account name uppercased; the account name must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$`. Accounts missing any required variable are dropped with a boot warning (boot never fails). Multiple accounts are supported.

Example:

```
EMAIL_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT=local
EMAIL_LOCAL_USER=agent@local.example
EMAIL_LOCAL_PASS=<credential>
EMAIL_LOCAL_IMAP_HOST=mail.local.example

dsh-email README · Config layer (cordis patch)：An optional config layer sits on top of the env block: a patch entry targeting the plugin id `dsh-email` (the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, the user-global `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml`, or a `--patch` overlay) carries a `config` object whose keys are camelCase mirrors of the env fields - `defaultAccount`, `readBodyLimit`, and `accounts` (a map of account name to `user`, `pass`, `imapHost`, `imapPort`, `imapSecure`, `imapAllowInsecureTls`, `smtpHost`, `smtpPort`, `smtpSecure`, `smtpAllowInsecureTls`, `from`, `fromName`, `sentFolder`, `sentFolderAutocreate`, `allowDelete`, `timeoutMs`, plus the trigger fields `triggerEnable`, `triggerPrompt`, `triggerFolder`, `triggerIdleMs`, `triggerMaxConcurrent`, `triggerQueueMax`, `triggerPreset`, `triggerReasoningEffort`). Every key is optional.

dsh-email README · Config layer (cordis patch)：- One precedence chain: delivered value > env value > built-in default; keys the layer omits resolve as the env block, so `config: {}` (or no entry) is exactly the env-only behavior.
- A patch targets a row by id and replaces its whole config - no deep merge, so a layer that overrides one field restates the fields it keeps (layer order: the plugin's own default entry, the profile patch, the user-global patch, any `--patch` overlay).
- The layer is validated before the plugin starts: an unknown key or an out-of-range value fails the plugin entry at load; incomplete account data only warns, as in the env block.
- With the live patch reload, editing the patch file re-runs the plugin without a restart; otherwise the change applies at the next restart.
- The agent edits the patch file as a plain file operation under its own permissions; the plugin provides no tool for changing its own configuration. The `accounts` verb shows values only.

dsh-email README · New mail trigger：With `EMAIL_<N>_TRIGGER_ENABLE=true` (plus a `TRIGGER_PROMPT`), the plugin keeps one resident IMAP connection on that account: it opens `TRIGGER_FOLDER` read-only (EXAMINE) and listens. New mail reaches it two ways - the server's untagged EXISTS (IDLE, or the library's NOOP polling on servers without IDLE) and a heartbeat resync every `TRIGGER_IDLE_MS` that recomputes the folder's UNSEEN set (the sole repair for a lost event or count drift, and the probe that detects a half-open connection). Both trigger the same action: dispatch a fresh agent session per new UNSEEN message.

EMAIL_DEFAULT_ACCOUNT=local
EMAIL_LOCAL_USER=agent@local.example
EMAIL_LOCAL_PASS=<credential>
EMAIL_LOCAL_IMAP_HOST=mail.local.example

dsh-email README · New mail trigger：Each session receives a minimal prompt, laid out static-first: a type label naming account + folder, the `TRIGGER_PROMPT` verbatim under a `Policy:` block and the execution-rules pointer line, then the dynamic layer - one envelope line (`uid | INTERNALDATE | From: | Subject:`) and the message body as a `Body:` block (the first text part, else the first html part, capped at the read-body budget `EMAIL_READ_BODY_LIMIT` - omitted when the message has no text / html part or the body fetch degrades, in which case the prompt ends at the envelope line). The session's execution rules (get the body, act on the policy, mark the message seen, summarize) live in the skill's "Trigger session" section.

dsh-email README · New mail trigger：- Dispatch state: up to `TRIGGER_MAX_CONCURRENT` sessions run at once; newer mails wait in a FIFO queue of at most `TRIGGER_QUEUE_MAX`; beyond that the overflow is a visible log entry and the mail simply stays UNSEEN (retried on a later resync).
- Session route: each trigger session is created with the deployment's default model route when one resolves; `TRIGGER_REASONING_EFFORT` sets the session's reasoning effort (closed set, absent = the framework provider default), passed through to the framework's agent options.
- Mark-seen is the session's job (via the `email` tool), not the watcher's. A session that settles without marking seen (or whose dispatch failed) is re-dispatched on the next resync - an idempotent replay, the designed behavior.
- Failure modes all fail visible and self-heal: connect / command failures close the connection and reconnect through an exponential backoff (5s x 2, capped at 60s), then resync on the fresh connection (new mail that arrived in the meantime is picked up); a queue overflow, a failed dispatch (agents service missing, unresolvable preset, turn error) and a missing EXAMINE folder are visible log entries. dsh-email README · Session offload：Trigger sessions leave on-disk session logs in the framework session store; at trigger-mail volume the store grows without bound. The per-minute offload sweep archives settled trigger sessions once the account's retention window elapses, so the store stays bounded: the store is never deleted, only moved, a session that is still running is kept until it settles, and a removed account is offloaded immediately regardless of age. The retention window and the per-sweep budget are the `SESSION_RETENTION` and `EMAIL_OFFLOAD_BATCH` settings in the table above (window syntax included). An unreachable persistence service, a missing store root, or an archive on a different mount disables the sweep for that round (a visible warning; log lines are never lost); a failed individual move is retried next round.
dsh-email README · Usage：The plugin adds the `email` tool and the `dsh-email` skill (verb reference, env contract details, limits, troubleshooting). The sixteen verbs, one line each:

dsh-email README · Usage：```
email { verb: "accounts" }                                  # configured accounts (local, no network)
email { verb: "verify" }                                    # live connectivity + credentials, zero side effects
email { verb: "folders" }                                    # mailbox names
email { verb: "list", flagged: true }                       # newest-first summaries, flagged only

dsh-email README · Usage：Reads never change server-side flags; `mark` is the only way to write flags. Failures carry an error code for transport origins (`auth` / `network` / `tls` / `timeout` / `protocol` / `server`); local validation errors carry none.

dsh-email README · Limits and boundaries：- Stateless verbs: one fresh connection per call; no connection pooling. Per-event push exists only through the new-mail trigger watcher (one resident connection per enabled account; accounts without it keep exactly the stateless footprint).
- No subscribe/unsubscribe verbs, no folder management beyond create/delete; no XOAUTH2 (password / app-specific password only).
- `delete` and `delete_folder` are fail-closed: they run only on accounts with `EMAIL_<N>_ALLOW_DELETE=true`; `move` is ungated because a failed source-side deletion leaves the copies in the destination.
- Read bodies are truncated to the configured budget; `save_part` retrieves full parts.
- Sent messages are not recalled; a SENT_FOLDER copy that fails on a missing folder first tries to create it (unless `EMAIL_<N>_SENT_FOLDER_AUTOCREATE=false` or the folder is exactly INBOX), then retries once; a copy failure that survives that is reported without rolling back the delivered message.
